prose: An Australian tutoring business told parents to stop paying for human tutors and put the money into Gemini or ChatGPT subscriptions instead - then closed down. Dymocks Tutoring and Talent 100, which runs five centres across Sydney, shuts at the end of the week after telling customers that AI has rendered its service obsolete.

The company is pointing at a real shift: students increasingly use AI for exam preparation and instant study feedback. A tutoring company declaring its own human service obsolete - rather than being displaced quietly - makes this an unusually blunt data point in the AI-and-education debate. (The Sydney Morning Herald original sits behind its paywall; this summary is based on the article's freely available first section.)
highlights: Dymocks Tutoring and Talent 100 (five Sydney centres) closes this week, declaring itself obsolete
It advised parents to invest in Gemini or ChatGPT rather than 'overpriced' human tutors
Students increasingly use AI for exam prep and immediate study feedback
A business publicly attributing its own closure to AI is a rare, blunt case in education
Summary based on the article's free section; the SMH original is paywalled
